BACKGROUND (possibly unreachable from your worktree): agent-io/prds/kbu-community-analysis-v1/fullprompt.md, committed on wip. Do not rely on it; this prompt is the authoritative spec.

REPO CONTEXT YOU NEED.
KBUtilLib uses a composition architecture. Each domain module defines TWO classes:
a legacy implementation class inheriting from KBModelUtils, and an `*Impl` wrapper that
holds `env` plus sibling `*Impl` instances, constructs the legacy delegate inside
try/except, and exposes `available` / `unavailable_reason` / `__dir__` / `__getattr__`.
Read src/kbutillib/domains/modeling/ms_fba_utils.py (class MSFBAUtils near the end of the
file, and class MSFBAUtilsImpl at the very end) and copy that shape exactly.
The facade src/kbutillib/toolkit.py exposes each module as a lazy property with a private
`_name = None` backing field set in __init__ and a local import inside the property body.
GitHub-only dependencies are declared in dependencies.yaml at the repo root and resolved
with kbutillib.core.dependency_manager.get_dependency_path(name), which returns a Path or
None and never raises. See src/kbutillib/domains/thermo/thermo_predictors/base.py
(function dependency_repo_path) for the worked example.
Tests live under tests/<domain>/. tests/conftest.py provides a `mini_model` cobra fixture
and a `kbutillib_app` facade fixture.

UPSTREAM CONTEXT YOU NEED (https://github.com/ModelSEED/MSCommunity, tip 2dcff16f8e20a5b2a2acbb28b60a8ad38ec924fc, 2026-09-23).
The pin is a FLOOR: before b14f50f (2026-09-01) a float abundance raised TypeError in
MSCommunity.__init__ and gapfill's solver string landed on MSGapfill's atp_gapfilling
positional, silently running an ATP gapfill. Do not develop against an older checkout.
The package is `mscommunity`. Relevant surface:
  mscommunity.commhelper.build_from_species_models(org_models, model_id=None, name=None,
      abundances=None, standardize=False, MSmodel=False, commkinetics=True,
      copy_models=True, climit=None, o2limit=None, printing=False) -> cobra.Model
      It copies each member model and rewrites compartments: member i (1-BASED) gets
      intracellular compartment c{i}; the extracellular compartment is SHARED as e0;
      member biomass reactions are renumbered bio2, bio3, ...
  mscommunity.mscommsim.MSCommunity(model=None, member_models=None, abundances=None,
      ids=None, kinetic_coeff=750, flux_limit=300, probs=None, climit=None, o2limit=None,
      lp_filename=None, printing=False, eleLimits=None, ID=None,
      close_member_drains=False)
      Attributes: .members (DictList of CommunityMember with .id, .abundance,
      .primary_biomass, .biomass_cpd, .index), .abundances, .util (MSModelUtil),
      .solution, .comm_growth, .memGrowths, .member_fluxes, .exchange_fluxes,
      .suboptimal_solution, .primary_biomass.
      Methods: set_abundance(abundances), set_objective(target=, targets=, weights=,
      minimize=), constrain(element_uptake_limit=, thermo_params=, msdb_path=),
      run_fba(media=None, pfba=False, fva_reactions=None), predict_abundances(media=None,
      pfba=True, timeout=60, environName=None, regularization=True,
      update_abundances=False, determinize=False, qp_backend=None),
      micom(media, tradeoff=0.6), gapfill(media=, target=, ...),
      test_individual_species(media=, interacting=, run_atp=, run_biomass=),
      interactions(...), to_sbml(export_name), print_lp(filename=),
      extract_problem(), solve_batch(instances, backend="cpu", ...).
  mscommunity.mscommviz has MODULE-LEVEL functions wrongly decorated with @staticmethod
      at lines 37, 84, 99 and 252: run_fba, abundance_variability_analysis, interactions,
      visual_interactions. staticmethod objects are only directly callable on Python
      3.10+; KBUtilLib supports >=3.9. ALWAYS call them through the _unwrap helper.
      mscommviz.interactions(mscommodel, solution=None, media=None, flux_threshold=1,
      msdb=None, msdb_path=None, visualize=True, filename='cross_feeding',
      export_format="svg", node_metabolites=True, show_figure=True, ignore_mets=None)
      returns a tuple (cross_feeding_df, exchanged_mets_df) of pandas DataFrames.

CRITICAL HAZARD. modelseedpy ALSO ships a class named MSCommunity at
modelseedpy/community/mscommunity.py. It is an older, DIVERGED copy exported by
`from modelseedpy.community import *`. It shares most method names, so importing the wrong
one produces plausible WRONG NUMBERS rather than an error. Everything in this PRD must
guard against it.

STYLE. Match the surrounding code: type hints, Google-style docstrings, module-level
logger, `__all__`. Do not reformat files you are not otherwise editing.

YOUR TASK: create the module skeleton, the dependency gate, and the pure helpers.

1. Add to dependencies.yaml (repo root), under `dependencies:`, matching the existing
   indentation and style:
       mscommunity:
         path: "../MSCommunity"
         git: "https://github.com/ModelSEED/MSCommunity.git"
         commit: "2dcff16f8e20a5b2a2acbb28b60a8ad38ec924fc"
       escher_edit:
         path: "../editEscher"
         git: "https://github.com/ModelSEED/editEscher.git"
         commit: "6474698c67e8b9a1e8ab44c38686b27821d20389"
   ALSO add to pyproject.toml a new optional-dependencies group:
       community = ["beautifulsoup4", "lxml"]
   Those are escher_edit's only required deps and they ARE on PyPI; the package itself is
   GitHub-only and resolves through dependencies.yaml. Do NOT add shapely or pandas --
   escher_edit lists them as extras and nothing this module calls needs them.
   The `commit` key is NEW -- no other entry carries one. Confirm that
   DependencyManager._load_config ignores unknown keys (read it) so this stays additive,
   and do NOT change DependencyManager in this task.
   Add a module-level constant PINNED_MSCOMMUNITY_COMMIT holding that SHA, and have
   _import_mscommunity() compare it best-effort against the resolved checkout's HEAD
   (read .git/HEAD / .git/refs, or shell out to git rev-parse inside try/except). On a
   mismatch, log a WARNING naming both SHAs. NEVER raise and never refuse the import:
   pinning here is for visibility, not enforcement, so a developer working ahead of the
   pin is not blocked.

2. Create src/kbutillib/domains/modeling/ms_community_utils.py containing:

   __all__ = ["MSCommunityUtils", "MSCommunityUtilsImpl", "CommunityModel",
              "CommunityFBAResult", "CommunityMapArtifacts", "CommunityDependencyError",
              "CommunitySolverError", "CommunityVisualizationError"]

   a) Three exception classes deriving from KBUtilLib's EXISTING hierarchy in
      src/kbutillib/core/errors.py -- read that file first. NOT bare Exception:
        CommunityDependencyError(BackendUnavailableError)   # BackendUnavailableError
                                                            # subclasses KBUtilLibError and
                                                            # is what the cheminformatics
                                                            # and thermo backends already
                                                            # raise for this condition
        CommunitySolverError(KBUtilLibError)
        CommunityVisualizationError(KBUtilLibError)   # a rendering dependency missing, or
                                                   # a map with no drawable members

   b) `_unwrap(fn)` -> returns fn.__func__ when isinstance(fn, staticmethod), else fn.
      Docstring must explain the Python 3.9 staticmethod hazard.

   c) `_import_mscommunity()` -> module or None. NEVER raises.
      Step 1: try `import mscommunity`.
      Step 2: on ImportError, call get_dependency_path("mscommunity") (imported lazily
      inside the function, best-effort inside try/except). If it returns a path that
      contains a `mscommunity` subdirectory with an __init__.py, insert str(path) at
      sys.path[0] and retry the import.
      Step 3: PROVENANCE GATE, with BOTH sides bound so the allowlist is neither too
      strict nor too lax. Resolve the MSCommunity class and:
        ACCEPT when MSCommunity.__module__ starts with "mscommunity." -- this admits
          mscommunity.mscommsim.MSCommunity and any future re-export inside that package;
        REJECT otherwise, and specifically when it starts with "modelseedpy".
      On rejection return None; the caller reports it unavailable.
      Cache the result in a module-level variable so repeated calls are cheap, and provide
      a `_reset_mscommunity_cache()` for tests. Keep _import_mscommunity importable at
      kbutillib.domains.modeling.ms_community_utils._import_mscommunity -- tests patch
      sys.modules against it.

      Step 4: COMMIT PIN CHECK, described under item 1 above. Warn, never raise.

   c2) `_import_escher_edit()` -> module or None. NEVER raises. Same shape as
      _import_mscommunity with TWO differences that matter:
        - THE PATH IS DIFFERENT. editEscher is a src/ layout: the repo is `editEscher`, the
          distribution is `escher-edit`, and the import is `escher_edit` under `src/`. So on
          the dependencies.yaml fallback you must insert `<path>/src` into sys.path, NOT
          `<path>`. Getting this wrong gives a confusing ModuleNotFoundError on a checkout
          that is present and correct. (MSCommunity is flat, so it gets the repo root.)
        - NO PROVENANCE GATE. Nothing else in the ecosystem exports the name `escher_edit`,
          so the Q3 hazard does not exist here. Do not add a gate.
      Carry its own PINNED_ESCHER_EDIT_COMMIT constant and the same warn-on-mismatch.
      Add `_escher_edit_unavailable_reason()` alongside the MSCommunity one.

   d) `_mscommunity_unavailable_reason()` -> str | None. Returns None when available, else
      one of two specific strings: one naming that the mscommunity package is not
      importable and not resolvable via dependencies.yaml, and one CONTAINING THE LITERAL
      PHRASE "the superseded copy", built as:
      "resolved MSCommunity is modelseedpy.community.MSCommunity (the superseded copy), "
      "not the standalone mscommunity package" followed by the module path ACTUALLY
      resolved. Tests assert on that phrase, so keep it stable.

   e) `normalize_abundances(abundances: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]` — pure.
      Divides by the sum. Raises ValueError on an empty mapping or a non-positive total.

   f) `project_member_fluxes(fluxes, member_index, member_biomass_id=None)` — PURE, no
      cobra import. Signature: (Mapping[str, float], int, str | None) -> dict[str, float].
      `member_index` is 1-based (member i lives in compartment c{i}).
      Rules, applied to each (reaction_id, flux) pair:
        - an id ending in "_c{member_index}" -> rewritten to end in "_c0", kept;
        - an id ending in "_c{j}" for any other integer j -> DROPPED;
        - an id ending in "_e0" (including EX_ reactions) -> kept unchanged;
        - an id equal to member_biomass_id (e.g. "bio3") -> renamed to "bio1", kept;
        - any other "bio<digits>" id -> DROPPED;
        - anything else -> kept unchanged.
      Use a compiled regex for the compartment suffix; do not use str.replace, which would
      corrupt an id containing the pattern mid-string.

   g) Two frozen-ish dataclasses (use @dataclass, not frozen, so callers can annotate):
      CommunityModel(mscomm: Any, member_ids: list[str], abundances: dict[str, float],
                     source_model_ids: dict[str, str], kinetic_coeff: float,
                     abundances_were_supplied: bool = False)
        plus a method `member_index(member_id) -> int` returning the 1-based index,
        raising KeyError with a message listing the known member ids when absent.
      CommunityMapArtifacts(map_json: Path, svg: Path | None, html: Path | None,
                     n_members: int, n_compounds: int, n_blocks: int)
      CommunityFBAResult(status: str, trustworthy: bool, community_growth: float,
                     member_growth: dict[str, float], exchange_fluxes: dict[str, float],
                     fluxes: Any, media_id: str | None,
                     kinetics_relaxed: bool = False, notes: list[str] = field(default_factory=list))

   h) `class MSCommunityUtils(KBModelUtils)` with only __init__ for now (accepting **kwargs
      and calling super().__init__(**kwargs)), and a module docstring in the style of
      ms_fba_utils.py that pins the upstream MSCommunity APIs this module relies on.

   i) `class MSCommunityUtilsImpl` following MSFBAUtilsImpl exactly:
      __init__(self, env, model, fba, escher, biochem, **kwargs) storing each as a private
      attribute with a read-only property; building the delegate in try/except;
      `available` returns False when the delegate is None OR
      _mscommunity_unavailable_reason() is not None; `unavailable_reason` returns the
      dependency reason first, then the delegate reason; plus __dir__ and __getattr__.

3. Create tests/modeling/test_ms_community_utils.py with tests that need NEITHER
   MSCommunity NOR a solver:
   - _unwrap returns the underlying function for a staticmethod and is identity otherwise.
   - _import_mscommunity returns None cleanly when the package is absent and
     get_dependency_path yields nothing (monkeypatch both).
   - THE PROVENANCE GATE: build a fake module object whose MSCommunity class has
     __module__ == "modelseedpy.community.mscommunity", inject it into sys.modules,
     and assert _import_mscommunity() returns None and
     _mscommunity_unavailable_reason() contains "superseded copy". This is the most
     important test in the file.
   - normalize_abundances({"a": 3, "b": 1}) == {"a": 0.75, "b": 0.25}; ValueError on {}.
   - project_member_fluxes: with member_ids A,B and member_index=2,
     {"rxn00001_c2": 5.0, "rxn00002_c1": 1.0, "EX_cpd00027_e0": -3.0, "bio3": 0.4} and
     member_biomass_id="bio3" yields exactly
     {"rxn00001_c0": 5.0, "EX_cpd00027_e0": -3.0, "bio1": 0.4}.
   - CommunityModel.member_index round-trips and raises KeyError listing known ids.
   - MSCommunityUtilsImpl constructed with a forced-None delegate reports available False
     with a non-empty reason, and raises RuntimeError on an unknown attribute.

DO NOT modify toolkit.py, kbutillib/__init__.py or any README in this task.

The dependencies.yaml mscommunity entry carries path, git and commit keys, and _import_mscommunity logs (never raises) on a commit mismatch. CRITICAL HAZARD. modelseedpy ALSO ships a class named MSCommunity at

STYLE. Match the surrounding code: type hints, Google-style docstrings, module-level

YOUR TASK: implement construction and simulation on MSCommunityUtils in
src/kbutillib/domains/modeling/ms_community_utils.py. The module skeleton, the dependency
gate, the exceptions, the dataclasses and the pure helpers (_unwrap, _import_mscommunity,
normalize_abundances, project_member_fluxes) already exist from the previous phase — READ
THEM FIRST and build on them; do not re-create them.

Add these methods to class MSCommunityUtils. Decorate each public one with
@capability(domain="community", summary=..., tags=...) following ms_fba_utils.py. Import
every mscommunity symbol lazily inside the method or a small private accessor, never at
module scope, so `import kbutillib` never requires mscommunity, cobra or graphviz. Raise
CommunityDependencyError with _mscommunity_unavailable_reason() when the package is absent.

CONSTRUCTION
  build_community(member_models, abundances=None, model_id=None, name=None,
                  kinetic_coeff=750, element_limits=None, printing=False,
                  build_solver="glpk", final_solver=None) -> CommunityModel
    - PASS close_member_drains=(abundances is not None) to MSCommunity, and record it on
      the handle. It is DERIVED, never a free parameter: saying "these are the abundances"
      is the same statement as "make them bind". Upstream's rule, verbatim from
      mscommsim.py: set it True "whenever the declared abundance vector is meant to BIND --
      any run where you read member growth rates or a kinetic coefficient off the
      solution." With the drain open a member synthesises biomass and discards it, so its
      biomass flux exceeds abundance*bio1 and the CommKinetics right-hand side inflates
      with it; upstream measured 83% of one member's biomass leaving through the drain.
    - Forward build_solver / final_solver to build_from_species_models unchanged. Upstream
      populates the merged model under GLPK and does one clean rebuild at the end because
      incremental constraint addition into optlang's Gurobi interface is superlinear.
    - `member_models` accepts cobra models, MSModelUtil objects, or workspace refs;
      resolve each through self._check_and_convert_model and self.get_model exactly as the
      rest of the modeling domain does.
    - Capture each input model's id BEFORE the merge, into source_model_ids. This is the
      whole point: build_from_species_models copies and RENAMES the models, so after the
      call there is no way to recover which input became which member.
    - Normalize `abundances` with normalize_abundances when supplied; when omitted leave it
      to upstream (uniform) and read the resulting comm.abundances back.
    - Construct mscommunity.mscommsim.MSCommunity(member_models=..., abundances=...,
      kinetic_coeff=..., ID=model_id, eleLimits=element_limits, printing=printing).
    - member_ids is [m.id for m in comm.members] IN COMMUNITY INDEX ORDER; assert it is
      consistent with each member's .index so member_index() is trustworthy.
  load_community(id_or_ref, ws=None, member_ids=None) -> CommunityModel
    - Loads a previously saved community model via self.get_model and wraps it as
      MSCommunity(model=..., ids=member_ids).
    - Recovery order, and all three routes must be tried before raising:
        1. model.notes["kbutil.community"] -- our own JSON blob, which also restores
           source_model_ids, abundances and kinetic_coeff;
        2. the explicit member_ids argument;
        3. upstream's model.notes["member_biomass_cpds"].
      When none is available RAISE ValueError naming all three. Do not guess.
      A handle rebuilt from route 2 or 3 has an EMPTY source_model_ids; that is expected,
      and render_member_map reports it as a named ValueError rather than a traceback.
  save_community(comm, workspace=None, objid=None, suffix=None)
    - BEFORE saving, write our own provenance onto the model:
        model.notes["kbutil.community"] = json.dumps({"schema_version": 1,
            "member_ids": [...], "source_model_ids": {...}, "abundances": {...},
            "kinetic_coeff": ..., "abundances_were_supplied": ...})
      as a JSON STRING -- workspace notes values are not reliably structured.
      This is load-bearing, not bookkeeping: build_community captures member_ids and
      source_model_ids precisely because upstream destroys them, and without persisting
      that capture a save/load cycle throws it away again, after which render_member_map
      cannot resolve a member's source model.
    - Save through the existing self.save_model path as an ordinary KBaseFBA.FBAModel. Do
      NOT invent a new workspace type: a community model IS an FBA model, and a new type
      would be invisible to every tool that already reads models.
  export_community_sbml(comm, path) -> Path, delegating to comm.mscomm.to_sbml.

SIMULATION
  run_community_fba(comm, media=None, pfba=False, min_member_growth=0.0)
                    -> CommunityFBAResult
    - There is deliberately NO fva_reactions argument. Upstream accepts one but its result
      shape is unspecified and CommunityFBAResult has no field for it; callers who need it
      use comm.mscomm.run_fba(..., fva_reactions=...) through the escape hatch.
    - Resolve a media id or name through self.get_media when `media` is not already a
      media object. Set result.media_id to the resolved object's id, or to the literal
      string "<model-default>" when media is None. Provenance is the point: a result that
      cannot say what medium produced it cannot be compared with another.
    - WRAP THE DELEGATE CALL IN contextlib.redirect_stdout. MSCommunity announces its most
      consequential silent behaviour by print(), not by raising or by any flag: on a
      zero-growth community predict_abundances removes the _commKin constraints, re-solves,
      and PROCEEDS with the constraint-free result, printing "Kinetic constraints disabled
      for ...". Scan the captured text for that marker and for "doesn't grow", re-emit
      matches through logging, append them to result.notes, and set
      result.kinetics_relaxed True when the kinetics marker appears. Log non-matching
      captured output at DEBUG and discard it. This also stops upstream's print noise
      landing uninvited in a notebook. Add a test asserting the marker strings against the
      literal text in mscommsim.py so an upstream wording change fails loudly rather than
      silently ceasing to set the flag.
    - min_member_growth maps to upstream's SteadyCom-style floor. Default 0.0 means NO
      floor — upstream's historical default of 1 never actually reached the LP, so
      enforcing one by default would silently change every existing result. When it is
      positive, install the per-member constraint inside the model's context manager so it
      does not leak onto the caller's model, exactly as mscommviz.run_fba does.
    - Build the result from comm.mscomm after the solve: status from the cobra solution,
      trustworthy = not comm.mscomm.suboptimal_solution, community_growth from
      comm.mscomm.comm_growth, member_growth from comm.mscomm.memGrowths, exchange_fluxes
      from comm.mscomm.exchange_fluxes, fluxes = the solution's flux Series.
    - A sub-optimal LP MUST NOT raise. Upstream logs and continues; surfacing it as
      trustworthy=False is the entire reason CommunityFBAResult exists.
    - OVER-SPECIFICATION REFUSAL: when min_member_growth > 0 AND the community was built
      with caller-supplied fixed abundances (CommunityModel already carries the boolean
      `abundances_were_supplied` from the previous phase; SET it in build_community),
      raise CommunitySolverError BEFORE solving. The message must name
      both inputs and state that dropping either one resolves it. Rationale: fixing
      composition while also imposing a per-member growth floor over-determines the
      system, and an infeasible LP is a far worse message than a named refusal.

      delegating, snapshot EXACTLY TWO THINGS -- restoring too little leaves hidden
      mutation and restoring too much fights upstream's own bookkeeping:
        (a) the comm.mscomm.abundances mapping;
        (b) the {metabolite: coefficient} stoichiometry of the SINGLE COMMUNITY primary
            biomass reaction, comm.mscomm.primary_biomass -- the only reaction
            set_abundance touches. Members' own primary_biomass reactions are NOT modified
            by set_abundance and must NOT be snapshotted.
      In a finally block, restore both with add_metabolites(..., combine=False) unless
      update=True.
    - Pass update_abundances=update through to upstream.
    - Returns None when upstream returns None (a community that does not grow). Do not
      convert that into an exception.

      comm.mscomm._QP_CAPABLE, it does not exist. Fall back to testing
      optlang.available_solvers against gurobi / cplex / osqp / hybrid only if upstream

      names those four. Do not let optlang raise from inside the tradeoff loop.

      member id with the solo/interacting growth columns upstream produces.

      test_individual_species(interacting=False) reads ZERO GROWTH FOR EVERY MEMBER,
      silently and with no error: it disables the other members, which zeroes bio1, and
      bio1 is then the only outlet for the tested member's biomass because its drain is
      shut. Upstream fixed this for _solo_max_batch, which restores the target's drain from
      the biomass_drain_bounds snapshot taken at construction (mscommsim.py:886-888), and
      did NOT fix it for test_individual_species, which has no drain handling at all
      (mscommsim.py:387-400). Read both before implementing.
      So when comm.mscomm.close_member_drains is True AND interacting is False, restore
      every member's drain bounds from member.biomass_drain_bounds INSIDE the model's
      context manager (`with comm.mscomm.util.model:`) before delegating, so they revert
      automatically on exit. Record in the returned DataFrame's .attrs that drains were
      reopened for the measurement, so a solo growth rate is never silently compared with a
      coupled one.
      predict_abundances and regularization go through _solo_max_batch and are already
      safe; do not add a guard there.

                    solver="glpk") -> the integrated gapfill solution from upstream.
    - Upstream fixed the solver argument in b14f50f: it used to be passed as MSGapfill's
      7th positional, which is atp_gapfilling, so a truthy solver string silently ran an
      ATP gapfill instead of the requested one. Against the pinned tip the keyword path is
      correct; do not reintroduce a positional call.

  cross_feeding_table(comm, result=None, media=None, flux_threshold=1.0, msdb=None,
                      msdb_path=None, ignore_mets=None) -> tuple[DataFrame, DataFrame]

  fluxes_by_member(comm, result=None, min_abs_flux=0.0) -> dict[str, dict[str, float]]
    - THE ADAPTER between the two packages, and PUBLIC on purpose: it is the seam, and the
      first thing to inspect when a figure looks wrong.
    - Obtain cross_feeding_df via cross_feeding_table. Its index is compound ids (upstream has
      already stripped the trailing _e0) and its columns are the member ids PLUS a column
      literally named "Environment".
    - For each MEMBER column build {compound: flux} from the non-zero cells, dropping cells
      whose abs() is below min_abs_flux. APPLY NO SIGN FLIP: escher_edit documents
      "negative = consumed, positive = excreted", and MSCommunity fills each member column
      from that member's net flux, branching on < Zero for consumption and > Zero for
      donation. The conventions already agree -- this was verified against both sources, so
      do not "fix" it.
    - DROP the "Environment" column entirely. escher_edit derives its own input and output
      columns from which members consume and produce each compound; passing Environment
      through as a member would draw the medium as an organism. A member left with no
      compounds maps to {}.

  render_community_map(comm, result_or_results, output_path, *, min_abs_flux=0.0,
                       skip_amino_acids=False, member_groups=None, member_legend=None,
                       style=None, svg=True, html=True, map_name=None)
                       -> CommunityMapArtifacts
    THE PRIMARY COMMUNITY FIGURE. Three stages:
    1. `result_or_results` is either one CommunityFBAResult or a {label: result} mapping. For
       each, call fluxes_by_member then escher_edit.build_member_reactions(fbm,
       model_id=<label or "">, compound_names=..., min_abs_flux=min_abs_flux,
       skip_names=DEFAULT_SKIP_NAMES if skip_amino_acids else None).
    2. escher_edit.build_escher_map(blocks, compound_names=..., map_name=..., style=style).
       Pass blocks as [(label, members), ...] when SEVERAL results were given and as a BARE
       MEMBER LIST when one was. Write the returned [header, body] to output_path as JSON.
    3. When svg: escher_edit.render_map_svg(escher_map, out_path=<output_path with .svg>,
       dashed=True, layout=style, html=html, member_colors=<the mapping below>,
       member_groups=member_groups, member_legend=member_legend).

    THREE THINGS THAT ARE EASY TO GET WRONG AND EACH FAILS SILENTLY:

    (a) BUILD THE COLOUR MAPPING EXACTLY ONCE, from comm.member_ids, and pass the SAME
        mapping to every render:
            colors = escher_edit.palette.member_colors(comm.member_ids, groups=member_groups)
        escher_edit assigns palette slots from the members present in the map it is drawing,
        so per-condition maps built independently DISAGREE about which member is blue. Its own
        documentation says to build one mapping for a series. Passing member_colors=True would
        re-derive it per map.
    (b) COMPOUND NAMES DO NOT COME FROM THE DATAFRAME. interactions() builds a
        "Metabolites/Donor" display-name column and then DROPS it, so cross_feeding_df carries
        bare cpd##### ids. Resolve {compound_id: name} through the biochemistry sibling already
        on the Impl (self.biochem) for the union of compounds across all conditions, and FALL
        BACK to using ids as their own names when biochem is unavailable -- a map reading
        cpd00027 is worse than one reading D-Glucose and far better than no map. Never raise
        for this.
    (c) PASS THE SAME MapStyle INSTANCE to build_escher_map(style=) and render_map_svg(
        layout=). The layout reserves room for labels at the style's sizes; rendering with a
        different style draws text the layout did not allow for.

    Raise CommunityVisualizationError when _import_escher_edit() returns None (naming
    escher_edit and its dependencies.yaml entry), and when build_escher_map raises ValueError
    for having no drawable members -- translate that into a message saying the community
    produced no above-threshold exchanges at the given min_abs_flux.
    skip_amino_acids defaults to False: silently hiding metabolites from a figure someone will
    interpret is not a default anyone should get without asking.
    Return CommunityMapArtifacts(map_json, svg, html, n_members, n_compounds, n_blocks) with
    svg/html None when not requested.

  render_member_map(comm, member_id, map, output_path, result=None, media=None,
                    **escher_kwargs) -> Path
    - UNCHANGED from the earlier design and retained deliberately: the community map has one
      net organism reaction per member and NO intracellular reactions, so it cannot answer
      "what is this member's metabolism doing".
      1. i = comm.member_index(member_id)  (1-based).
      2. Flux mapping from result.fluxes, else run run_community_fba(comm, media=media).
      3. The member's biomass reaction id from
         comm.mscomm.members.get_by_id(member_id).primary_biomass.id.
      4. projected = project_member_fluxes(fluxes, i, member_biomass_id=<that id>).
      5. Resolve the member's SOURCE single-species model from
         comm.source_model_ids[member_id] via self.get_model. Use the SOURCE model, NOT the
         community model: Escher maps are keyed on single-organism ids (_c0 / _e0), which is
         what the projection produces.
      6. self.escher.create_map_html2(source_model, map, output_path, flux=projected,
         **escher_kwargs).
    - Inject a banner naming the member id, community id, media id, community growth rate and
      the sentence "Projected member view: fluxes are this member's slice of a community
      solution. EX_ exchange reactions are community-level and cannot be attributed to one
      member." Implement the injection as a small private helper with its own test; insert it
      after the opening <body> tag, and prepend if no <body> is found rather than failing.
    - Raise KeyError for an unknown member_id and ValueError when source_model_ids has no
      entry for it (a community rebuilt by load_community's fallback routes will not have one).

                      -> networkx.DiGraph
    - Built FROM the cross-feeding DataFrame. One node per member plus a node literally named
      "Environment" -- this one DOES keep it, because it is a graph of exchange rather than a
      drawing. One directed edge per donor -> consumer transfer of a metabolite, with edge
      attributes `metabolite`, `flux` (signed) and `abs_flux`; an edge runs from each producer
      to each consumer of the same metabolite. Drop edges below min_abs_flux. Import networkx
      lazily and raise CommunityDependencyError if absent.

dropped from the design: escher_edit draws the same relationships better and needs no `dot`
binary. Do not import graphviz, do not call shutil.which("dot"), and do not call

  - render_member_map raises ValueError naming the member when source_model_ids lacks it.
  - cross_feeding_graph from a hand-written frame produces the expected nodes and directed
